questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had never visited, but heard a lot of great things about Vienna.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There was a general introduction seminar, which was okay. There was also an international office, with limited opening hours, but very helpful and kind people. Lastly there was also an introduction seminar at juridicum which was far to late.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: As I said you could go to the international office yourself, and the mandatory introduction seminars.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy enough. Start in good time and you can find some good and cheap places.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Some districts are better then others, 4. 5. and 7. was my favorites.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Very DIY. You have to put together your own schedule, which is quite complicated, as you have to attend a lot of classes (each only being worth between 2 and 4 ECTS points), and most if not all classes have mandatory attendance, meaning that you have to spend quite some time electing classes.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: As I said a seminar at juridicum, but which took place after the deadline. There also was some help to find online.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It took some time, but I was somewhat satisfied.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Registrer for as much as possible, then you can always deregister later. Also if you are put on the waitlist for a class you want, you will basically always get the spot, if you just show up for the first class.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: A bit lower in general then in Copenhagen, it was however very dependent on the teacher.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Almost no group work, mostly lectures, with involvement of student. But again very dependent on the teacher, with some having far more student interaction, and some classes being totally different.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Israel, the Westbank & Gaza, Republicanism: From Aristotle to John McCormick, Mediation for Lawyers, Introduction to English Contract and Tort Law, Introduction to Chinese Legal History, Cinema and Human Rights, International Law and the Use of Force, International Criminal Law and its Enforcement and The Practice of International Dispute Settlement.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Mediation for Lawyers was a very fun and diffrent class, mostly being build around roleplaying exercises. i learned quite a bit from both International Criminal Law and its Enforcement and The Practice of International Dispute Settlement, but International Law and the Use of Force was definitely the most interesting class in my opinion.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Fees from registration at the municipality.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Most things were cheaper than in Denmark, but don't expect, as cheap prices as other places especially in southern or eastern europe.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Non that was very suitable for Erasmus students in my opinion, but one or two of my friends from Erasmus did join some sport activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Non really, especially if your German isn't that good.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel to other european cities, visit museums and see an opera. Definitely go and do a heuringer when possible. It's basically an hike in the wine fields on the outskirts of the city, where you make stops along the way at different stands, where the farmers sell the new wine.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, it's not very diffrent, or though a bit more religious.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really, Austrians aren't the friendlies people in the world, but that isn't exactly what the Danes are famous for either. There is some cultural differences with the other Erasmus students as well, so be open minded.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The wine, and the use of nature.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go to as many Erasmus events as possible at the beginig of the stay, so that you make other Erasmus friends. Make sure to experience some of the history and culture by going to stuff like the museums and the opera. Vienna is also a great hub for traveling, so do that.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware that juridicum is quite a horrible building with no windows in the classroms and way too few spaces for studying.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus friends from all over Europe I made.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having so many classes at the same time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Your system is terrible, I filled this thing out for the third time now, as it keeps login me off, without saving the things I wrote. If you make this kind of thing mandatory, at least have some systems that actually work.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
